## Observation

`rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot._list_submodules` runs `git ls-tree -r --full-tree <sha>` through `git_fetch.git_run` and parses stdout without checking the return code. A failed or watchdog-killed `ls-tree` (300 s `_GIT_TIMEOUT`) yields empty stdout, so it answers "no submodules".

Both materialization paths in `acquire` persist that answer through `_store_caveats` into `<sha>.caveats.json`. A cache hit reads the sidecar and never recomputes, so one failed call permanently records "no submodule caveats" for that immutable SHA.

Impact today is limited: no production code outside `repo_snapshot.py` reads `SnapshotHandle.submodules`. The persisted record is still wrong, and any future reader would trust it.

Found by code reading while fixing educatory-toxic-eel (same class: a git outcome read as an answer). Not reproduced; the eel's test wrapper (a `git` shim that execs `sleep` for one subcommand under a 1 s bound) can drive it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_list_submodules` distinguishes a failed or timed-out `ls-tree` from an empty gitlink list (timeout recognised with `git_outcome.is_watchdog_timeout`).
- [x] A failed or timed-out listing is not persisted to the caveats sidecar as "no submodules".
- [x] A regression test drives the timeout and asserts the sidecar does not record an empty submodule list.
